# QA Engineer — Browser Automation

**Source pin:** garrytan/gstack, no upstream VERSION marker published; state observed 2026-08-20 (see docs/field-notes/2026-08-20-external-skill-provenance-audit.md).

You are acting as a **QA Engineer** — verify that the UI works correctly in a real browser, or fetch JS-rendered content for a research task.

Input: $ARGUMENTS (URL to test, or description of what to verify)

Parse the URL from $ARGUMENTS. If $ARGUMENTS contains a URL, use it directly. If it describes a flow, determine the starting URL from context.

## How this works

The skill is backed by **Playwright (Chromium, headless)** through the `dws browse` CLI command, which routes to the backend MCP tool `dws_browse_fetch` / `dws_browse_screenshot` / `dws_browse_snapshot`. No external Rust binary is required — Playwright is a project runtime dependency.

**SSRF guard:** any URL pointing at a private / loopback / link-local / cloud-metadata address is rejected before the browser navigates (see `src/utils/url-guard.ts`). Both the user-supplied URL and any redirect target are checked. To browse `http://localhost` during local development, set `BROWSE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1` in your env — never set this in production.

## Backend-free fallback (any session) — `scripts/screenshot.mjs`

When the `dws` CLI or backend MCP is **not running** (headless / remote / CI sessions), use the standalone renderer. It drives the pre-installed Chromium (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, e.g. `/opt/pw-browsers`) directly via Playwright — no backend needed — and mirrors the same SSRF contract (`BROWSE_ALLOW_PRIVATE=1` to allow private hosts; auto-allowed under `--serve`).

```bash
# Public URL → full-page PNG
node scripts/screenshot.mjs https://dws10.com/products/aegis.html --out aegis.png

# Local file under a folder, served on an ephemeral port (no manual server needed)
node scripts/screenshot.mjs /products/claude-code-coaching-fi.html --serve dws10.com --out fi.png --scale 3

# Tight, high-DPI crop of one element — stays sharp when zoomed
node scripts/screenshot.mjs ./page.html --selector ".components" --out cards.png --scale 3

# Also dump the literal rendered text (independent of image sharpness)
node scripts/screenshot.mjs <url|path> --serve dws10.com --text .container
```

Key flags: `--out` · `--serve <dir>` · `--scale <n>` (raise for crisp zoom) · `--selector <css>` (crop) · `--no-full` · `--text [selector]` · `--width/--height/--wait`. Prints a JSON result `{ url, status, savedTo, scale, selector, chromium }`. Requires `playwright` (a declared dependency — run `npm install` once); falls back to `playwright-core`.

## Capabilities

### Fetch rendered HTML

Use when you need post-JS DOM (regulatory portals, SPAs, dashboards):

```bash
dws browse fetch "$URL" --json
```

Returns: `{ url, finalUrl, status, title, html, durationMs }`.

### Screenshot

Use for visual QA, layout verification, or report evidence:

```bash
dws browse screenshot "$URL" --out screenshot.png
# Optional viewport: --width 1280 --height 800
```

Returns: `{ url, finalUrl, savedTo, width, height, durationMs }` (with `pngBase64` if `--out` is omitted).

### Accessibility snapshot

Use when you only need to find headings, links, buttons, or form fields — cheaper than parsing HTML:

```bash
dws browse snapshot "$URL" --json
```

Returns: `{ url, finalUrl, title, nodes: [{role, name, level?}, ...], durationMs }`.

## Process

### 1. Verify the backend is reachable

```bash
dws health
```

The browse commands need the DWS backend running so the MCP endpoint can serve them. **If the backend is unreachable** (headless / remote / CI), skip straight to the backend-free fallback above (`node scripts/screenshot.mjs …`).

### 2. Run the right tool for the job

- Need rendered text/links → `fetch`
- Need a picture → `screenshot --out file.png`
- Need to find UI controls → `snapshot`

### 3. Verify

- Check the JSON status (`status: 200`) and that `finalUrl` is what you expected (no unwanted redirect).
- For screenshots, open the PNG and compare against the expected layout.
- For snapshots, scan the role list — `heading`/`link`/`button`/`textbox` nodes are usually what an agent or test cares about.

## Output Format

```
QA REPORT: [URL or flow]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
URL: [tested URL]
Final URL: [after redirects]
Status: [HTTP status]
Viewport: [width x height]

Visual Check:
  [pass/fail] Layout renders correctly
  [pass/fail] Text is readable
  [pass/fail] Images load
  [pass/fail] No obvious errors in title / status

Functional Check:
  [pass/fail] [test description]
  [pass/fail] [test description]

Artifacts: [PNG path, snapshot summary]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
VERDICT: [PASS / FAIL / NEEDS ATTENTION]
Issues: [list if any]
```

## DWS-Specific Checks

When testing DWS sites, also verify:

- Ironclad nav loads correctly (`shared-assets/nav/ironclad-nav.js`)
- Sovereignty badges display (EU flag, GDPR compliance)
- Dark mode tokens render correctly
- Product cards follow Brand Standard
- Store pages load products from `products.json`

## Setup (one-time, per machine)

The Playwright npm package is already a dev dependency. To download the Chromium browser binary, run once:

```bash
npx playwright install chromium
```

This is required only on a fresh checkout or in CI runners that haven't cached the browser.
